title.narrative: Somaliland Termination Oppression of women and girls Programme II (STOP II)

description.narrative: Provide a description of the proposed action and its relevance, including all the information requested below, referring to the overall objective and specific objective(s), as well as to the expected results (i.e. impact, outcome(s), possible intermediary outcomes and outputs:i.Briefly outline the relevance of the action to the objectives/sectors/themes/specific priorities of the call for proposals and to the particular needs and constraints of the target country/countries, region(s) (including synergy with other development initiatives and avoidance of duplication)Somaliland (and Somalia) have been jointly ranked as one of the worst countries worldwide for women in terms of violence and exclusion of women (UNDP 2012), second only to Afghanistan. The prevalence of sexual gender based violence (SGBV) in Somaliland is consistently higher than the global average. 98% of the women and girls have been subjected to the most severe type of female genital mutilation (FGM) according to UNICEF. Research by Health Poverty Action (HPA) in 2018 noted prevalence of rape at 66%, with a majority of the respondents concluding that Pharaonic (most severe form) FGM, rape and forced marriage were the most prevalent forms of GBV. With no formal census conducted, the population is estimated at 5 million people with approximately 100,000 living in internally displaced peoples (IDP) camps, average life expectancy of 52.8 years and literacy rates of 36% for women and 44% for men. Somalilands GDP per capita, at just $348 (310), makes it the fourth-poorest country in the world. Its main industry is livestock export, which accounts for about 70% of jobs. Nearly 40% of the rural population and 30% of those living in urban areas are living below the international poverty line (World Bank 2012). Decades of civil unrest have resulted in a large diaspora with remittances from these making up 34% of the GDP, cushioning the lives of some 80% unemployed citizens. (UNDP, 2014).The two districts of Burao and Ainabo will be the focus of this action. Burao is the regional capital of Togdheer region, one of the six administrative regions of Somaliland. Togdheer region, with an estimated population of 754,378 is the second most populous in Somaliland next only to Hargeisa. (UNFPA 2017). Ainabo on the other hand is located in the Sool region, the poorest and the least developed region of Somaliland, with the least number of health facilities, educational facilities and other social amenities (Sool Development plan).
